requirements.note: 4-across square centre-cropped grid with 2pt gaps, oldest at top, opens scrolled to the newest at the bottom, day headings in full form ("Monday, October 26, 2026") and a photo-count footer.
Tap opens the photo at its own aspect ratio; swiping left and right pages through photos, with a position counter ("1497 of 1,500"); swiping down closes it.
A heart toggle in the viewer's bottom bar favorites and unfavorites; a white heart appears on the grid thumbnail straight away.
Albums tab with a large title, a 'My Albums' heading and a 2-column grid of all 8 albums with rounded covers and counts; each opens a grid with a back button and Select.

Select mode shows blue checkmarks, dims selected tiles and puts the count in the title; batch favorite works (then leaves select mode); batch delete asks for confirmation in an alert and removes the photos; the counts update.
Batch favorites, a viewer favorite and a 2-photo deletion all survived a relaunch (1,498 Photos).

tells: At the largest text size the nav bar's subtitle ('1,498 Photos') grows huge and pushes the shrunken 'Library' title into the top-left corner; the header looks broken rather than like a system title/subtitle.
Day headings always include the year and never use 'Today'/'Yesterday'; Photos drops the year for the current year and uses relative days.
Batch delete confirms with a centred alert rather than an action sheet or popover anchored to the trash button.
Fast flings travel noticeably less far than a stock UICollectionView (three flings went about 3 weeks back, versus about 7 weeks in B); momentum feels damped.
Album covers are exposed to accessibility as 'Link' elements and thumbnails as plain buttons, which reads web-like.
No Share button in the viewer or in select mode.
A tall footer leaves a large empty band above the tab bar at the bottom of the library.
The viewer shows an 'N of 1,500' counter in the toolbar, which Photos doesn't do.
A.scroll: Smooth, with no blank tiles or pop-in even on hard flings, but deceleration is short, so long flings cover much less ground than a native collection view. Pulling past the top and bottom bounces normally.

requirements.note: 4-across square centre-cropped grid with thin gaps, oldest at top, opens at the newest at the bottom; day headings use Photos-style relative and short dates ('Yesterday', 'Sunday, October 25'); footer shows photo and favorite counts.
Opens full screen at its own aspect ratio, centred on screen; swiping left and right pages through photos; swiping down closes it; date and time sit in the nav bar.
A heart button in the viewer toolbar (between Share and Delete) toggles favorite; a filled heart shows on the grid thumbnail.
Albums tab with a large title and a 2-column grid of the 8 albums with covers and counts; an album opens a grid with day headings, a back button, Select and a footer count.

Select mode shows checkmarks and the count in the title, with Share, Favorite and Delete in the toolbar; batch favorite keeps you in select mode, as Photos does; Delete opens a popover anchored to the trash button ('Delete 2 Photos').
Favorites and deletions survived a relaunch (1,498 Photos · 84 Favorites).

tells: The viewer's toolbar buttons sit in separate glass circles instead of one grouped toolbar; minor.
Tiles drawn under the translucent nav bar blur only part of the bar in some positions (the left half shows photo colour, the right is plain); a cosmetic scroll-edge oddity.
B.scroll: Feels like a native collection view: long flings with full momentum, no blank tiles or pop-in, and sticky day headings that pin cleanly under the nav bar. Bouncing at both ends is normal.

why: Both apps meet all six requirements and look almost the same. B is closer to Photos in the details: relative day headings, a delete popover anchored to the button, Share, staying in select mode after a batch action, and native-feeling fling momentum. A's damped scrolling, centred delete alert and broken nav-bar subtitle at the largest text size give it away.
